cutList.label: Top
cutList.derivation: A 3/4 plywood top, 42 x 22 x 3/4 (note 2.2 item 1): length across X 42 x 1024 = 43008, width up Y 22 x 1024 = 22528, thickness 3/4 x 1024 = 768. No joint lengthens it: it receives four tabletop joints and is inserted into none.

cutList.label: Apron, back
cutList.derivation: 36 x 5 1/2 x 3/4: 39 - 2 x 1 1/2 between the legs = 36 (36864), width 5 1/2 (5632), thickness 768. No allowance. Pocket holes: joints J1 (contact 3/4 x 5 1/2, so max(2, ceil(5.5 / 2)) = 3) at each end from the inside (south) face; clips: one tabletop joint 36 long, max(2, ceil(36 / 12)) = 3, on the inside (south) face because the middle of the design is south of the apron.
joinery: Drill 3 pocket holes in the west end and 3 in the east end, from the south face.
Fit 3 tabletop clips along the top edge on the south face (slot or recess per the clip's instructions).

cutList.label: Front rail
cutList.derivation: 36 x 1 1/2 x 3/4 (1x2): 36864 x 1536 x 768. Pocket holes: J3 contact 3/4 x 1 1/2, max(2, ceil(1.5 / 2)) = 2 at each end from the inside (north) face; clips: 36 long -> 3, on the north face.
joinery: Drill 2 pocket holes in the west end and 2 in the east end, from the north face.
Fit 3 tabletop clips along the top edge on the north face (slot or recess per the clip's instructions).

cutList.label: Drawer front
cutList.derivation: 17 3/4 x 5 1/2 x 3/4 (1x6), two drawers: 18176 x 5632 x 768, quantity 2. Each is only the receiving part of one butt joint with screws (J10), which cuts nothing.

cutList.label: Web
cutList.derivation: 17 1/2 x 5 1/2 x 3/4: the 19 in between the aprons less the rail's and the apron's 3/4: 17.5 -> 17920 x 5632 x 768. Inserted in J4 (north end, contact 3/4 x 5 1/2 -> 3 pocket holes) and J5 (south end, contact 3/4 x 1 1/2 -> 2), both drilled from the west face (the builder's pick, the note's 6.2); the larger run is named first.
joinery: Drill 3 pocket holes in the north end and 2 in the south end, from the west face.

cutList.label: Leg
cutList.derivation: 2x2, 16 1/4 tall: 16640 x 1536 x 1536, quantity 4. A leg only receives butt joints, so nothing is done to it and the four legs list as one row whichever way they are turned.

cutList.label: Drawer bottom
cutList.derivation: Drawn 15 5/8 x 15 x 1/4 (16000 x 15360 x 256). Four 1/4 grooves (J9): two into the sides on the length, two into the box front and back on the width. Finished 16000 + 2 x 256 = 16512 (16 1/8) by 15360 + 2 x 256 = 15872 (15 1/2). Quantity 2.
joinery: Length includes 1/4" into a groove at each end; width includes 1/4" into a groove at each edge.

cutList.label: Drawer box front
cutList.derivation: Drawn 15 5/8 x 3 1/2 x 1/2 (16000). Rabbeted into both sides (J7): 16000 + 2 x 256 = 16512 (16 1/8), width 3584, thickness 512. Its north face is grooved for the bottom (J9): the bottom's edge is at z 11 1/2..11 3/4 in a box whose bottom edge is at 11, so 1/2 from the bottom edge and 1/4 wide, full length. Quantity 2.
joinery: Length includes 1/4" into a rabbet at each end.
Groove the north face: 1/4" wide, 1/4" deep, 1/2" from the bottom edge, full length.

cutList.label: Apron, side
cutList.derivation: 16 x 5 1/2 x 3/4: 19 - 2 x 1 1/2 = 16 (16384). Pocket holes at both ends (J2, contact 3/4 x 5 1/2 -> 3 each) from the inside face, which is the east face of the west apron and the west face of the east apron: turned end for end (a half-turn about the width axis) one is the other, so the two are one row of 2. Clips: 16 long -> max(2, ceil(16/12)) = 2 on the inside face.
joinery: Drill 3 pocket holes in the south end and 3 in the north end, from the east face.
Fit 2 tabletop clips along the top edge on the east face (slot or recess per the clip's instructions).

cutList.label: Drawer side, left
cutList.derivation: 16 x 3 1/2 x 1/2 (16384 x 3584 x 512), quantity 2 (drawers A and B). The left side's inside face is east. Rabbet (J7) at its front (south) end on the east face: 1/2 wide (the front's thickness), 1/4 deep. Groove (J9) on the east face: 1/4 wide, 1/4 deep, 1/2 from the bottom edge.
joinery: Rabbet the south end on the east face: 1/2" wide, 1/4" deep.
Groove the east face: 1/4" wide, 1/4" deep, 1/2" from the bottom edge, full length.

cutList.label: Drawer side, right
cutList.derivation: The mirror of the left side: the same size, but its inside face is west. No half-turn makes it the left side: the rabbet pins the front end and the groove pins the bottom edge, so it is its own row of 2 -- four identical sides with two of them wrong is the mistake this row separates.
joinery: Rabbet the south end on the west face: 1/2" wide, 1/4" deep.
Groove the west face: 1/4" wide, 1/4" deep, 1/2" from the bottom edge, full length.

cutList.label: Slide cleat
cutList.derivation: 1x2, 16 x 1 1/2 x 3/4: 16384 x 1536 x 768, quantity 2. Each only receives nothing and is inserted only in a butt joint with screws (J6), which cuts nothing.

cutList.label: Drawer box back
cutList.derivation: Drawn 15 5/8 x 3 1/2 x 1/2 (16000 x 3584 x 512), quantity 2: butted between the sides (J8, nothing cut) and grooved on its south face for the bottom (J9), 1/2 from the bottom edge.
joinery: Groove the south face: 1/4" wide, 1/4" deep, 1/2" from the bottom edge, full length.

shoppingList.derivation: Area of the parts, finished sizes (allowances in): 1785/4 in² against one 48" x 96" sheet = 4608 in²; ceil(area / 4608) = 1 sheet. By area, and so labelled a floor; no board feet for a panel.
Area of the parts, finished sizes (allowances in): 3999/8 in² against one 48" x 96" sheet = 4608 in²; ceil(area / 4608) = 1 sheet. By area, and so labelled a floor; no board feet for a panel.

Pieces, longest first: 36, 16, 16 (inches). Kerf rule (napkin's default 1/8 in per cut): a board with n pieces takes n cuts when an offcut remains, n-1 when the pieces and kerfs exactly fill it; used length = pieces + kerf x cuts. First-fit decreasing puts each piece on the first open board with room, opening new boards of the longest stocked length (192 in), then each board shrinks to the smallest stocked length (72, 96, 120, 144, 168, 192 in) that holds it. All three go on one board: 36 + 16 + 16 = 68 in; with 3 cuts of 1/8 in that is 68 3/8 in; 72 in (6') holds it (not an exact fill: 68 1/4 is not 72), offcut 72 - 68 3/8 = 3 5/8 in. So 1 × 6'-0". Board feet, nominal 1" x 2": bought 1.0, used 0.9, waste 0.1, each rounded once at the end. Finished sizes are used: the drawer parts are already lengthened by their joinery allowances.
